title: Fennhollow Botanical Soda summer campaign: neutralise two card-shot packshots to their grey card by eye, license four oversized lifestyle stock frames and grade the whole set to one warm-daylight white point by eye, correct the OFF-TEAL hero bottle to the house teal with a bounded in-family shift, reframe DOWN to exact web slots, and report the recipe
grounding_note: ADAPTED from a real Freelancer.com brief ("Vibrant Social & Web Graphics") in which the client wants "matching website graphics—hero images, section headers, and call-to-action spots—plus occasional banner ads" where every asset "should feel part of one cohesive family while being perfectly sized, compressed, and formatted for its destination," with deliverables including "Web-ready exports in the correct dimensions and file types" and a "Mini style reference (colours, typography) to keep future assets consistent." The real client name is NOT reproduced; the brand is laundered to a fictional small-batch craft-soda maker, "Fennhollow Botanical Soda," and the job is reasonably enriched into a runnable, gen-free, connector-only benchmark that honors the stock_hero_expand slot: the imagery is sourced by LICENSING oversized Adobe Stock frames and reframing DOWN to each web slot (never upscaled, never canvas-expanded), and the cohesion claim is made checkable by anchoring the campaign white point to two supplied packshots that each carry a physical grey card in frame. No real person, brand, product or trademark is named anywhere.
one_line_ask: Neutralise two differently-lit Fennhollow packshots to the grey card each carries (by eye), license four oversized lifestyle stock frames and grade every image by eye to one warm-daylight white point with no visible drift, correct the OFF-TEAL (bright aqua) hero bottle in the spotlight frame onto the deep muted house teal with a bounded hue nudge plus a desaturate-and-darken that keeps its glass and texture natural — while leaving the frame that already shows the correct teal bottle completely alone — reframe every image DOWN to its exact web slot size, vectorize and knock out the wordmark, and deliver a web pack plus a recipe note that reports the final per-image parameters you applied.
full_brief: Fennhollow Botanical Soda, a fictional small-batch craft-soda maker, is launching a summer campaign and needs a cohesive set of website and banner graphics built entirely from imagery we already have or can license — no from-scratch illustration, no AI canvas expansion, no upscaling. Two problems have to be solved together. FIRST, colour truth and cohesion. We are handing off two studio packshots of our signature teal bottle (product_studio_greycard.jpg and product_window_greycard.jpg). They were shot on two different days under different light — one under cool studio strobes, one by a warm window — so they do not match, and neither is colour-accurate as delivered. Each frame includes a physical 18% grey card in the corner. Use those cards: neutralise each packshot BY EYE until the grey card actually looks neutral grey, so the bottle's real teal is finally true-to-product. Those two corrected packshots then DEFINE the campaign's white point. SECOND, the lifestyle imagery. Source four bright, summery lifestyle frames from stock — a hand pouring fizz over ice, a picnic-table flat lay of fruit and a filled glass, a beach/porch bottle-in-hand shot, and a condensation close-up — and grade every one of them so the whole set (packshots + lifestyle) reads as ONE warm, energetic, daylight family. "Cohesive" here is not a vibe: we want no visible warm/cool drift between any two slots, sitting at the target look our corrected packshots establish, whites kept below clipping and blacks not crushed. Because the four lifestyle frames were lit differently from each other, the SAME slider settings will NOT make them match — each needs its own corrective push by eye to the shared target, and we want those final settings written down. THE CATCH: one of the lifestyle frames you'll find is gorgeous but the hero bottle in it is the wrong shade of our own colour family — a bright, light, slightly-too-cyan AQUA glass, not the deep muted teal of our actual SKU. Bring that bottle onto our house teal so it can front the product-spotlight slot. Because it is already in the blue-green family, this is a CONTROLLED move, not a far colour swing: a small nudge of the hue toward green plus a pull-down of saturation and brightness until the bright aqua settles into the deep, muted house teal you established from the corrected packshots. Do NOT attempt some dramatic rotation to a brand-new colour — the source is already close, so it is a bounded correction. And do it the way a real retoucher would: the glass highlights, the condensation, the label edges and the drink level must all stay natural. No flat dead-fill colour, no whole-image tint that bleeds onto the fruit and the table. Watch which bottle you touch: another lifestyle frame already shows a bottle in the CORRECT deep house teal and must be left completely alone — the two blue-green bottles look similar at a glance, so identify the off-shade aqua one and correct ONLY that. HARD SOURCING RULE (this is a website hero set): every licensed frame MUST be licensed at a resolution LARGER than the slot it feeds and then cropped/reframed DOWN — never scaled up, never canvas-expanded. If a tempting comp is smaller than its destination slot, reject it and license a bigger one; do not stretch or expand it to fit. Deliverables and EXACT sizes: two colour-true product tiles at 1080x1080 (from the corrected packshots); a desktop homepage hero at 1920x1080; a mobile homepage hero at 1080x1920 (from a SECOND, portrait source — not a squeezed desktop crop); a 'Summer Flavors' section header at 1600x600; a product-spotlight card at 1080x1350 (the corrected house-teal bottle, reframed with breathing room at the base for the dev team's live CTA); and a leaderboard promo banner at 1456x180 (subject reframed to keep the left region clear for a live wordmark overlay). The photographic slots stay clean of baked-in text and logo so the dev team overlays the live headline, CTA and wordmark on top. Also prepare the wordmark for them: knock out its background to a transparent PNG and vectorize it to a clean SVG so it stays razor-sharp at any size. Final handoff: a zipped web-ready pack (the seven sized JPEGs, the wordmark SVG, the transparent wordmark PNG) plus a one-page recipe note that lists the palette AND reports the EXACT final parameters you applied per image — the two grey-card neutralisation deltas, the four per-frame corrective grades to the target white point, and the two-pass HSL bottle-correction values — so future assets can be matched to this family.

inputs.name: product_studio_greycard.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal ecommerce packshot of a deep-teal glass craft-soda bottle with a clean matte paper label, standing on a seamless off-white sweep. A physical 18% neutral grey calibration card is propped in the bottom-right corner of the frame, clearly visible. Lit by cool studio strobes so the whole image has a slightly cool/blue cast and the grey card looks faintly blue; flat even lighting, real glass highlights and a soft contact shadow, un-graded straight-off-camera look. Roughly 3200x3200, sharp.
inputs.realism_notes: Colour-truth anchor #1. Deliberately cool white balance so the grey card visibly departs from neutral and the by-eye neutralisation step has real work; the grey card in frame makes the correction externally checkable by the grader. Shot ~3200px so the 1080x1080 tile is a crop DOWN. gpt-image-2 for photoreal glass + an accurate grey patch.

inputs.name: product_window_greycard.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal ecommerce packshot of the SAME deep-teal glass craft-soda bottle and matte label, on the same off-white sweep, with the same physical 18% neutral grey calibration card propped in the bottom-right corner. This time lit by warm afternoon window light so the whole image has a noticeably warm/amber cast and the grey card looks faintly orange; soft directional light, real glass highlights, soft shadow, un-graded look. Roughly 3200x3200, sharp.
inputs.realism_notes: Colour-truth anchor #2, shot under a DIFFERENT (warm) white balance than anchor #1, so the two packshots genuinely do not match and cannot be neutralised with identical settings. Same grey card lets the grader confirm the correction. Oversized vs the 1080x1080 tile.

inputs.name: fennhollow_wordmark.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat modern craft-beverage wordmark reading 'Fennhollow' in a friendly rounded bold sans-serif, solid brand-teal letters with a tiny amber leaf accent over the second 'n', sitting on a plain flat light-grey (non-transparent) background with generous margins. Crisp flat raster PNG, high contrast, no gradients, no photographic elements, clean edges suitable for background knock-out and vectorizing.
inputs.realism_notes: Supplied brand-kit wordmark. Given on a flat NON-transparent ground on purpose: the agent must knock the background out before tracing, or image_vectorize will return a filled rectangle. gemini-3-pro-image for clean legible single-colour lettering that vectorizes cleanly once prepped.

inputs.name: fennhollow_brandkit.txt
inputs.gen_prompt: Write a short brand-kit note for a fictional craft-soda brand named Fennhollow Botanical Soda. Include: palette (brand teal = a deep, muted blue-green; sunlit amber accent; cream); voice = bright, warm, botanical, energetic; the campaign white-point target = 'warm daylight, roughly a 5300-5500K feel, a gentle consistent warm push above neutral, whites held below clipping'; the cohesion tolerance = 'no visible warm/cool or brightness drift between any two delivered slots'; the web slots and EXACT pixel sizes (product tile 1080x1080, desktop hero 1920x1080, mobile hero 1080x1920, Summer Flavors section header 1600x600, product-spotlight card 1080x1350, promo banner 1456x180); the rule that the signature product bottle is the deep muted house teal (NOT a bright light aqua); and the rule that all photographic slots stay clean of baked-in text/logo so the dev team overlays the headline, CTA and wordmark live.
inputs.realism_notes: Normal client hand-off note carrying the palette, the campaign white-point target + tolerance, the deep-teal-SKU rule (distinguished from a bright aqua so the bottle correction has a clear qualitative target, not a pixel hex the agent must match by measuring), and the exact slot sizes the freelancer must honor. Consumed by the recipe-note step, not merge-bound.

inputs.name: stock_search_wishlist.txt
inputs.gen_prompt: Write a short shortlist of Adobe Stock search phrases a designer would use to source bright summery craft-soda lifestyle frames: e.g. 'hand pouring fizzy soda over ice close up', 'summer picnic table fruit and sparkling drink flat lay', 'person holding cold soda bottle beach golden hour', 'condensation on cold soda bottle macro'. State the hard sourcing rule verbatim: each frame must be licensed at a resolution LARGER than the web slot it will feed so it can be cropped DOWN, never scaled up or canvas-expanded; if a comp is smaller than its slot, reject it and license a bigger one — do not stretch or expand it to fit. Note that some pour candidates in the results feature a bright, light AQUA-glass bottle rather than the deep muted house teal, while other candidates already show the correct deep-teal bottle; the two blue-green bottles look similar at a glance.
inputs.realism_notes: Mirrors how a freelancer plans stock sourcing and encodes the oversized-then-crop-DOWN discipline as an explicit acceptance rule (the goal), leaving the agent to actually notice and reject an undersized comp under temptation. Flags that some pour candidates are off-teal aqua-bottle while others are already correct deep-teal — driving the in-family bottle-correction and the look-alike triage decision.

outputs.name: product_tile_studio_1080x1080.jpg
outputs.spec: Colour-true product tile, exactly 1080x1080, cropped DOWN from the corrected studio packshot after neutralising its cool cast by eye to the in-frame grey card (grey patch looks neutral, bottle teal true-to-product); web-ready sRGB JPEG. Acceptance (grader-checked): grey card reads neutral (R,G,B within a tight channel spread) and matches tile #2's white point/brightness.

outputs.name: product_tile_window_1080x1080.jpg
outputs.spec: Colour-true product tile, exactly 1080x1080, cropped DOWN from the corrected window packshot after neutralising its warm cast by eye to the in-frame grey card; must match tile #1's white point and brightness; web-ready sRGB JPEG. Acceptance (grader-checked): grey card neutral, no visible drift from tile #1.

outputs.name: hero_desktop_1920x1080.jpg
outputs.spec: Desktop homepage hero, exactly 1920x1080, cropped/reframed DOWN from an OVERSIZED licensed landscape pour/lifestyle frame; graded by eye to the campaign warm-daylight white point with no visible drift; clean of baked-in text/logo for live overlay; web-ready sRGB JPEG.

outputs.name: hero_mobile_1080x1920.jpg
outputs.spec: Mobile homepage hero, exactly 1080x1920 portrait, cropped DOWN from a SECOND oversized licensed portrait lifestyle frame (not a squeezed desktop crop); graded by eye to the same white point with no visible drift; clean for live overlay; web-ready sRGB JPEG.

outputs.name: section_header_1600x600.jpg
outputs.spec: 'Summer Flavors' section header, exactly 1600x600, cropped DOWN from an oversized licensed fruit/glass flat-lay frame; graded by eye to the same white point with no visible drift; clean for live overlay; web-ready sRGB JPEG.

outputs.name: product_spotlight_1080x1350.jpg
outputs.spec: Product-spotlight card, exactly 1080x1350, built from the oversized licensed pour frame whose hero bottle was the OFF-TEAL bright aqua: the bottle is corrected onto the deep muted house teal via two masked HSL passes — a BOUNDED adjacent-hue nudge toward green, then a desaturate-and-darken — that preserve glass highlights, condensation, label texture and drink level (no flat fill, no whole-image tint). This is a small controlled shift within the blue-green family, NOT a far rotation to a new hue. Then graded to the campaign white point and reframed DOWN with breathing room at the base for the dev team's live CTA; clean; web-ready sRGB JPEG. Acceptance (grader-checked): corrected bottle reads as the deep house teal (clearly distinct from its aqua source, consistent with the packshot bottle), texture intact; the separately-licensed already-correct teal-bottle frame is left unaltered.

outputs.name: promo_banner_1456x180.jpg
outputs.spec: Leaderboard promo banner, exactly 1456x180, cropped DOWN as a wide slice from the graded desktop-hero master, subject reframed to keep the left region clear for the dev team's live wordmark overlay; same grade; clean; web-ready sRGB JPEG.

outputs.name: fennhollow_wordmark_transparent.png
outputs.spec: Transparent-background PNG of the wordmark, background knocked out from the supplied flat PNG, for the dev team's live overlays and as the prepped source for vectorizing.

outputs.name: fennhollow_wordmark.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the Fennhollow wordmark, traced AFTER the background is knocked out and the art is cropped to its glyph bounds, so it is the lettering (not a filled rectangle) and stays razor-sharp at any placement size.

outputs.name: fennhollow_style_recipe_note.txt
outputs.spec: One-page recipe note listing the palette (teal/amber/cream) AND REPORTING the exact final parameters the agent applied per image: the two grey-card neutralisation deltas (temperature/tint/exposure) for the packshots, the four per-frame corrective grades to the campaign white point, the campaign white-point target + tolerance, and the two-pass HSL bottle-correction values applied (the hue-nudge degrees and the saturation/luminance deltas) to bring the off-teal aqua bottle onto the house teal — so the family can be reproduced and 'matched' is verifiable. This is an applied-settings log, not a measurement report; no read/recovered hex or channel values.

outputs.name: fennhollow_campaign_pack.zip
outputs.spec: Zipped web-ready pack: the seven correctly-sized JPEGs (two product tiles, desktop hero, mobile hero, section header, product spotlight, promo banner), the wordmark SVG, the transparent wordmark PNG, and the recipe note.

connector_workflow.note: Upload the two supplied packshots, the wordmark PNG, and the brand-kit + wishlist notes into the working project so the edits can run against real asset references.

Search Adobe Stock for bright summery lifestyle candidates per the wishlist (pour-over-ice, fruit/glass flat lay, bottle-in-hand golden hour, condensation macro); returns low-res comps with resolution metadata. The agent must screen candidates against the oversized rule and reject any comp whose native resolution is smaller than the slot it would feed — those cannot be used, because filling the slot from them would require upscaling or generative expansion, which is banned.

License and download the chosen landscape pour/lifestyle frame at full resolution, OVERSIZED vs 1920x1080 so it can be cropped DOWN. If the most attractive landscape comp is under 1920px wide, do NOT license it for this slot — pick a larger one; never expand up to size. This landscape frame is one that already shows the CORRECT deep-teal bottle and needs no colour correction on the bottle — do not touch its bottle colour.
License a SECOND, portrait-oriented lifestyle frame at full resolution for the mobile hero, oversized vs 1080x1920 (distinct source, not the desktop frame squeezed).
License the fruit/glass flat-lay frame at full resolution for the Summer Flavors header, oversized vs 1600x600.

License the pour/close-up lifestyle frame whose hero bottle is the OFF-TEAL bright AQUA glass at full resolution, oversized vs 1080x1350. This is the frame whose bottle will be corrected onto the deep house teal. TRIAGE: the landscape frame licensed in step 3 already shows the CORRECT deep-teal bottle and must be left alone — the two blue-green bottles look alike, so the off-shade aqua one (this frame) is the only one to correct.

Neutralise product_studio_greycard.jpg to its in-frame grey card BY EYE: judge the cool/blue cast against the grey patch, warm the temperature + trim tint toward neutral, correct exposure until the grey card looks like neutral 18% grey and the bottle's teal is true-to-product. Record the exact temperature/tint/exposure delta APPLIED — it becomes an entry in the recipe note. Full-image adjustment, no mask. The agent never reads a pixel value; it neutralises visually and reports what it dialed.

Neutralise product_window_greycard.jpg to its in-frame grey card BY EYE — but this frame is WARM, so the correction is the OPPOSITE sign of step 7: cool the temperature + trim tint the other way + match brightness so both packshots land on the same neutral white point. Applying step 7's settings here would over-cool it; this is why the two packshots need different deltas. Record this delta too.

Crop DOWN the corrected studio packshot to exactly 1080x1080, subject-aware on the bottle, excluding the grey card from the delivered tile. onSubjectClipping='extract' (never 'expand'); downscale-only from the ~3200px source.
Crop DOWN the corrected window packshot to exactly 1080x1080, matching framing and brightness to tile #1 so the two tiles read as a pair. onSubjectClipping='extract'; downscale-only.

Corrective grade of the landscape lifestyle frame BY EYE to the campaign warm-daylight target defined by the neutralised packshots: temperature/tint pushed to remove THIS frame's specific cast, a gentle warm lift to the target, exposure/contrast evened, whites held below clip, a modest vibrance so the fizz reads. These are this frame's OWN deltas — not copied from another frame. Record the settings applied for the recipe note.

Crop/reframe DOWN from the oversized graded landscape frame to exactly 1920x1080, kept clean for the dev team's live headline. onSubjectClipping='extract' (never 'expand'); downscale-only, never enlarging beyond source pixels.

Corrective grade of the portrait lifestyle frame BY EYE to the SAME campaign white point — but with its OWN temperature/tint/exposure deltas, because it was lit differently from the landscape frame. The target is shared; the settings are not. Record them.
Crop/reframe DOWN to exactly 1080x1920 portrait mobile hero (distinct source). onSubjectClipping='extract'; downscale-only.

Corrective grade of the fruit/glass flat-lay BY EYE to the shared white point with its own deltas so the 'Summer Flavors' strip belongs to the family; guard the whites on the glass and the cream table. Record them.
Crop/reframe DOWN to exactly 1600x600, kept clean for live overlay. onSubjectClipping='extract'; downscale-only.

On the off-teal aqua-bottle pour frame, semantically select just the aqua glass soda bottle ('the aqua glass soda bottle') so the colour correction is isolated to the bottle — NOT the fruit, ice, hand or table. Returns a maskURI. Triage check: this is the off-shade aqua frame; the separately-licensed already-correct deep-teal-bottle frame (step 3) must never be selected/corrected.

Masked correction pass 1 (consumes the frame + the mask): nudge the aqua/cyan hue band a BOUNDED amount toward green-teal inside the selection — a moderate adjacent-hue shift, well under 90 degrees, which is within image_adjust_hsl's real range because the source is already blue-green. Existing luminosity carries the glass highlights, condensation and drink level. Confined to the mask, so the fruit, ice and table keep their colours. Uses image_adjust_hsl because it is the ONLY masked recolor path — image_apply_color_overlay is whole-image with no mask (would tint the whole frame) and image_fill_area is a flat solid fill (the dead-fill the brief forbids). NOT a far amber-to-teal rotation; that is out of the tool's range.

Masked correction pass 2 (consumes the hue-shifted frame + the same mask): DESATURATE and DARKEN the selected bottle — drop saturation and lower luminance — so the bright light aqua settles into the deep muted house teal seen in the corrected packshots rather than a garish cyan or a muddy blue-grey, still riding the original luminosity so highlights, label texture and condensation stay natural. This desaturate-and-darken is squarely within image_adjust_hsl's range. Record the two-pass HSL values APPLIED (the hue-nudge degrees and the saturation/luminance deltas) for the recipe note.
Grade the corrected spotlight frame BY EYE to the shared campaign white point with its own temperature/tint/exposure deltas so it matches the family AFTER the bottle correction. Record them.

Crop/reframe DOWN to exactly 1080x1350, pushing the bottle high so the base stays clear for the dev team's live CTA button. onSubjectClipping='extract' (never 'expand'); downscale-only from the oversized source.

Crop DOWN a wide leaderboard slice to exactly 1456x180 from the SAME graded desktop-hero master (guaranteeing the banner matches the desktop hero exactly), reframing the subject to keep the left region clear for the dev team's live wordmark overlay. onSubjectClipping='extract'; downscale-only.

Knock the flat light-grey background out of the supplied wordmark PNG to transparency. This is both the deliverable transparent PNG AND the prepped source for vectorizing — tracing the raw PNG with its background still on would return a filled rectangle, so it must be knocked out first.
Crop the knocked-out wordmark to the tight bounds of the lettering (prep-before-trace) so the vector traces only the glyphs with no surrounding transparent margin.
Vectorize the prepped, knocked-out, cropped wordmark raster into a clean SVG of the lettering for razor-sharp placement/scaling by the dev team on the CTA and banner.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: fennhollow_brandkit.txt, studio_neutralized, window_neutralized, hero_desktop_graded, hero_mobile_graded, header_graded, spotlight_graded, spotlight_teal
connector_workflow.note: Emit the one-page recipe note: palette (teal/amber/cream) + the campaign white-point target and tolerance + the REPORTED final per-image parameters the agent applied (two grey-card neutralisation deltas, four lifestyle corrective grades, the two-pass HSL bottle-correction values) so the family is reproducible and the match is verifiable. Applied-settings log only — no read/recovered hex or channel values.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: product_tile_studio_1080x1080.jpg, product_tile_window_1080x1080.jpg, hero_desktop_1920x1080.jpg, hero_mobile_1080x1920.jpg, section_header_1600x600.jpg, product_spotlight_1080x1350.jpg, promo_banner_1456x180.jpg, fennhollow_wordmark.svg, fennhollow_wordmark_transparent.png, fennhollow_style_recipe_note.txt
connector_workflow.note: Zip the web-ready pack: seven correctly-sized JPEGs + wordmark SVG + transparent PNG + recipe note.

chaining_note: Strict output->input chaining throughout. asset_add_file(1) makes the supplied packshots + wordmark + notes real references; asset_search(2) fans out into four oversized licenses (3 landscape with the already-correct teal bottle, 4 portrait, 5 flat-lay, 6 off-teal aqua-bottle pour). The two supplied packshots are each neutralised BY EYE to their in-frame grey card with OPPOSITE-sign corrections (7 cool->neutral, 8 warm->neutral) then cropped DOWN to the two 1080x1080 tiles (9,10). Each licensed lifestyle frame gets its OWN corrective grade to the shared campaign white point before its exact-px crop DOWN: landscape 11->crop(12), portrait 13->crop(14), flat-lay 15->crop(16). The aqua spotlight frame runs the masked-correction branch: select_by_prompt(17) isolates only the off-teal aqua bottle, two masked image_adjust_hsl passes (18 consumes frame+mask for a bounded adjacent-hue nudge, 19 consumes the hue-shifted frame+same mask for a desaturate-and-darken) settle it onto the deep house teal, then a corrective grade(20) and the crop DOWN to 1080x1350(21). The promo banner(22) is a wide slice DOWN off the SAME graded desktop master(11) so it matches the desktop hero. The wordmark forks off the supplied PNG through a disciplined prep-before-trace chain: remove_background(23) -> transparent PNG deliverable AND prepped source -> crop_to_bounds(24) -> vectorize(25) -> SVG. The recipe note(26) consumes the brand kit + every graded/neutralised master to report the final per-image parameters the agent applied; local_zip(27) converges all eleven deliverable files into the pack. Every step after the search and the raw loads consumes a prior step's output; nothing free-standing.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon flagship: 27 connector calls, 10 distinct Adobe-server tools plus two local steps — above the >=10 calls / >=6 distinct-tool floor. Difficulty is DEPTH, not repetition: it is NOT one grade recipe applied N times. Two packshots need opposite-sign grey-card neutralisations by eye; four differently-lit licensed frames each need their OWN corrective delta to converge on one shared white point (identical settings provably will not match them); one frame needs a two-pass luminosity-preserving masked HSL correction of just its off-teal aqua bottle — a bounded adjacent-hue nudge plus a desaturate-and-darken onto the deep house teal, both moves squarely inside image_adjust_hsl's real range — while a look-alike frame that already shows the correct deep teal must be left untouched (triage). The wordmark needs a knock-out -> crop-to-bounds -> vectorize prep chain or it traces to a rectangle; every output must be cropped DOWN to an exact pixel size from an OVERSIZED source with no upscaling or canvas-expansion; and the agent must REPORT its final per-image parameters (settings it applied, never a measured value) so the match is checkable. It respects every hard limit: no generative expansion/fill, no text-to-image or from-scratch art (the wordmark is a supplied PNG only knocked-out and traced; the bottle is corrected in place, not regenerated), no upscaling/super-resolution, no object-removal-with-reconstruction, no compositing, no image_fill_area and no image_apply_color_overlay (the bottle correction runs entirely through masked image_adjust_hsl, the only masked recolor path), and crucially NO far near-complementary hue rotation (the corrected bottle starts already blue-green, so the move stays within the tool's bounded range).
hardness_rationale: Failure gate the agent can actually trip via a wrong DECISION, not a self-measurement: the two supplied packshots each carry a physical grey card and must be neutralised to it BY EYE (grey patch made to look neutral) with OPPOSITE-sign corrections, and the four licensed lifestyle frames — deliberately lit cool, warm, flat and golden-hour — must all be pushed by eye to the one warm-daylight campaign look the corrected packshots define; an agent that dials identical grade parameters into differently-lit sources, or copies one frame's deltas to another, leaves a visible warm/cool drift and the set will not match. The agent NEVER reads a pixel, hex or channel value — it judges by eye and REPORTS the temperature/tint/exposure/vibrance it APPLIED per image in the recipe note; the numeric tolerance is the GRADER's, acceptance (grader-checked): grey card neutral within a tight channel spread and no visible drift between slots. Human-hard elements: (1) cross-asset colour cohesion by eye across six differently-lit frames plus two card-neutralised anchors; (2) a two-pass luminosity-preserving masked correction of the OFF-TEAL hero bottle — a bright aqua already in the blue-green family — onto the deep muted house teal via a BOUNDED adjacent-hue nudge plus a desaturate-and-darken (both moves image_adjust_hsl can actually do; a far amber-to-teal rotation could not), keeping glass highlights, condensation and label texture natural with no flat fill and no whole-image tint bleeding onto fruit and table; (3) triage — two lifestyle frames both show blue-green bottles that look similar at a glance, but one is the off-shade aqua that must be corrected while the other already shows the correct deep house teal and must be left alone, and getting it backwards is invisible until inspected; (4) prep-before-trace discipline on the wordmark (knock-out -> crop-to-bounds -> vectorize, or it traces to a filled rectangle). Deliberate trap: an attractive but UNDERSIZED stock comp tempts the naive path to license it and upscale/generative-expand it up to the 1920-wide hero slot — a banned capability that fails the 'license oversized, crop DOWN, never expand' rule; the correct path rejects the small comp and licenses a larger source. A second trap is reusing one frame's slider settings across the others, which looks efficient but breaks cohesion; a third is reaching for a dramatic far hue rotation on the bottle (out of the tool's range) instead of the small in-family correction the source actually needs. Acceptance (grader-checked): every output at its exact listed pixel size cropped DOWN from an oversized source (no upscaling); both packshots neutral to their grey card; all seven photographic slots free of visible warm/cool or brightness drift from the campaign look; the spotlight bottle reading the deep house teal with intact texture and clearly distinct from its aqua source; and the recipe note reporting the final per-image parameters the agent applied.
reverify: {"severity": "pass", "banned_capability_check": "CONFIRMED none of the banned capabilities are used.
